The report titled, 'Unprotected: The Detention of Palestinian Teenagers in East Jerusalem,’ is based on 60 affidavits of boys aged 12 to 17 arrested between January 2014 and August 2016. Each minor’s account of abuse tells a similar tale, pointing to a “primary mode of conduct adopted by the State of Israel for boys suspected of stonethrowing,” as stated in the report. The majority of boys interviewed were pulled out of bed in the middle of the night, handcuffed and interrogated before speaking to a lawyer and not informed of the right to remain silent. When in custody the: minors experienced physical abuse such as being beaten with sticks or batons. Additionally, they faced verbal insults from police officers who called them "dog" (Kalbi) during questioning. The report also highlights that many boys were subjected to prolonged periods of solitary confinement and exposure to harsh lighting conditions in order for the authorities to break their willpower without any consideration given towards maintaining a child's psychological well-being. The use of such tactics is considered by human rights experts as forms of cruel, degrading or unusual punishment. The document also points out that Palestinian minors were often detained on suspicion alone and not charged with an offense until long after the arrest was made – sometimes up to several months later - which violates international law regarding child detention. Moreover, these children are frequently held in adult prisons where they face further psychological trauma due to their isolation from family members. To determine if oral anticoagulation alters the association between vitreous hemorrhage (VH) and retinal tears in eyes with acute, posterior vitreous detachment (PVD). In this retrospective chart review, the complete records of consecutive patients with spontaneous, symptomatic acute PVD from a single referral-based practice were reviewed. The use of oral anticoagulants, the presence of a VH, and the presence of a retinal tear or detachment were recorded. A totalof 1054 eyes in 1000 patients met study criteria with at least one year follow-up (mean [SD], age =73 years; male=551). Of these cases: 24% experienced VH and/or RTE, while the remaining had PVD without either of those complications. A total of fourteen percent were on warfarin therapy for an average duration between five to six months prior or at diagnosis. Results: Oral anticoagulation (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·94; confidence interval[CI]:1-3) was not associated with increased risk in developing vitreous hemorrhage. However, the presence of a VH and RTE appeared to be significantly higher among those on oral anticoagulants compared without it (adjusted OR =2:95 [CI], 0·97–4; P=3). This association remained present even after adjusting for other variables such as age or comorbidities. Discussion: Our study suggests that the use of an oral anticoagulation may increase risk in developing vitreous hemorrhage and retinal tears among patients with acute posterior vitreous detachment. However, more rigorous studies are needed to validate these findings before clinicians could make informed decisions regarding treatment options for their patient population. Diffusion weighted images (DWI), from which the corresponding diffusion tensor images (DTI) are estimated, are commonly acquired with anisotropic discretizations. Traditional methods to up-sample diffusion weighted images generally rely on scene-based interpolation and do not exploit structural information from the images. In this study, a DTI up-sampling framework is presented that incorporates the underlying anatomical shape information by means of non-rigid inter-subject registration. This approach leverages the structural consistency across subjects to guide the up-sampling process, thereby enhancing the resolution and fidelity of the DTI data. texts.full_text: major depression. Unipolar and bipolar depression are known to exert detrimental effects on learning and memory processes. However, few comparisons have been undertaken between bipolar and unipolar patients with comparable illness histories, and predictors of impairment are not well understood. Adult outpatients with unipolar major depressive illness (UP, n = 30) and bipolar disorder (BP, n = 30), group-matched for illness duration and severity of depressive symptomatology (16% clinically remitted, 42% partially remitted, 42% depressed), and 30 demographically matched controls completed measures of general cognitive functioning as well as specific memory tasks. The results indicated that both the UP and BP groups exhibited significant deficits in verbal learning (immediate recall) compared to healthy control participants; however, these impairments were more pronounced among individuals with bipolar disorder. In terms of working memory performance on digit span forward/backward tests, only patients from the BD group showed a deficit relative to controls. Furthermore, while both clinical samples displayed impaired delayed free and cued-recall scores indicative of consolidation difficulties or retrieval deficits in long-term storage processes; these were again more severe for those with BP compared to UP. Notably, among all participants who had experienced at least one episode within the past six months (regardless if currently depressed), there was a trend suggesting that recent affective episodes may exacerbate memory problems. However, this relationship did not reach statistical significance after controlling for potential confounders such as medication use and comorbid anxiety disorders. Overall findings suggest distinct patterns of cognitive dysfunction between unipolar major depression versus bipolar disorder which could have implications regarding differential diagnosis or treatment strategies targeting neurocognitive symptoms in each condition separately
